title: The Table Between Centuries
brief: Five over-the-shoulder encounter posters; historical listener softly out of focus, seated Andre sharply focused and actively explaining with a distinct gesture.

posters.name: César — o peso do poder
posters.label: CHAPTER I — JULIUS CAESAR
posters.prompt:
Create ONE highly creative, finished theatrical character-encounter poster for the historical time-travel short film THE TABLE BETWEEN CENTURIES. Portrait 2:3 canvas. This must feel like a gripping candid moment from a prestige feature film, with one believable physical camera viewpoint and live human interaction.
REQUIRED CAMERA AND PERFORMANCE: An intimate OVER-THE-SHOULDER shot from immediately BEHIND the historical interlocutor who is SEATED in the near RIGHT foreground, facing Andre across the table. Their cloth-covered shoulder/back/upper arm provides a softly out-of-focus near frame, approx 20–28% of the width, substantial enough to register a seated person. Entire historical head and face are OUT OF FRAME beyond the upper/right crop; NO visible profile, nose, mouth, jaw, eyes, reflection or portrait. Do NOT substitute blur for hiding their face: it must be physically outside the frame. Andre is SEATED opposite in the LEFT/CENTRAL middle distance, in sharp focus from mid-torso upward with both forearms and gesturing hands visible. Frame his face large enough to recognize him. He looks toward the listener, just to camera-right, NEVER toward the camera. Catch him genuinely mid-explanation: lips slightly parted in a natural speaking shape, expressive eyebrows, leaning into the conversation and making the specific gesture below. Not a posed silent portrait, not clasped hands, not standing, not pointing at the viewer. Natural finger anatomy and two hands only for Andre; hands stay away from his face.
REFERENCES: Image 1 is Andre's REAL identity photograph: preserve his face proportions, hairline, actual age, short dark hair with grey at temples, brown/hazel eyes and short salt-and-pepper beard. Image 2 is the film keyframe: use his modern mid-grey subtly pinstriped jacket and white finely striped open-collar shirt, with no tie, and the era's cinematic atmosphere; CHANGE the static listening pose into active speaking. Image 3 is ONLY a historical costume/material reference for the near shoulder; do not copy its camera angle, head fragments, visible printed text or brands. Image 4 anchors the same pale weathered oak table, ring stain and chipped edge in every era. Preserve the real-photo identity over any synthetic reference drift. No beautification that changes anatomy, no generic actor, no aging-down.
DESIGN: Photorealistic 35mm cinema photography, physically convincing shallow depth of field, subtle halation and film grain, rich tactile materials, deliberate negative space. One scene only, no floating giant heads, no split-face collage, no multiverse portal, no clocks, no battle, explosions or crowds. Only these two seated people; Andre is the ONLY visible face. Use sophisticated, striking restrained typography with real movie-poster hierarchy. Exact text, all legible: star billing "ANDRE ATHAR"; main title "THE TABLE BETWEEN CENTURIES" (four words, may be stacked); the chapter label specified below. Main title dominates the lettering without covering Andre's face or hands. No other text, dialogue, fake credits, reviews, release dates, laurels, brands, watermark, mockup or borders. The output is the complete designed poster.

CAESAR / THE WEIGHT OF POWER. A sunlit private Roman atrium, red ochre fresco wall, weathered travertine columns, creamy wool with Tyrian-purple border at Caesar's near-right shoulder as in reference 3. Camera seated eye-level behind that shoulder; slightly diagonal tabletop leads directly to Andre. Andre leans forward, mid-sentence, right hand OPEN palm-up about 20 cm above the table with naturally separated curved fingers, left hand softly touching the tabletop, explaining a consequential point with confident concern. No aggressive finger point. The purple-trimmed shoulder is softly blurred, Andre's attentive eyes and expressive hand sharp. A single sharp bar of late Mediterranean sunlight crosses the red wall and catches airborne dust, warm skin with deep wine-red shadows, quietly ominous architecture. A small wax tablet lies CLOSED near Caesar, no writing. Art direction: rich oxblood, limestone, warm brass, black. Title in exceptionally refined ivory Roman serif, stacked in the lower 20% over gently darkened tabletop, with tiny chapter label CHAPTER I — JULIUS CAESAR below. ANDRE ATHAR widely tracked at the top. Show the suspense of a man explaining the future to power, not an emperor propaganda portrait.

correction.reason: Unrequested background human bust violates zero-other-faces constraint.
correction.prompt:
Edit this exact completed film poster. Change ONE detail only: remove the human bust/statue on its pedestal behind Andre at upper-right centre. Replace the entire bust and pedestal with an unobtrusive plain red-ochre plaster wall continuation and natural light/shadow, consistent with the existing Roman architecture. Absolutely no human sculptures, portraits, busts, faces or reflections in the background.
Preserve everything else: Andre's exact face/likeness, expression, open gesturing right hand and resting left hand, seated pose, grey pinstripe suit and striped shirt; the soft-focus cream-and-purple near-right foreground shoulder; the weathered table; camera framing; lighting; colour; all existing title typography, ANDRE ATHAR billing and CHAPTER I — JULIUS CAESAR lettering with identical spelling and placement; portrait 2:3. The historical interlocutor's head remains fully outside the frame. Do not recompose or redesign the poster. Output the full corrected poster, not a crop.

GENGHIS KHAN / WHAT AN EMPIRE JOINS. Inside a large dark campaign ger: layered felt, wood lattice, taut roof cords disappearing into darkness; the SEATED near-right listener's broad fur-edged dark-brown silk/leather lamellar shoulder, antique bronze studs from reference 3, is softly out of focus. Absolutely no weapons or visible historical head/face. Slightly lower seated camera, shooting just over his shoulder so Andre feels engaged rather than dwarfed. Andre is leaning in and actively explaining the scale of something: BOTH hands raised low over the tabletop, palms angled inward and about 35 cm apart, a natural measured spreading gesture, fingers relaxed, eyebrows lifted, lips parted, looking at Khan. Keep hands distinct and realistic, not splayed toward the lens. Warm ember glow from low left and a narrow blue-grey shaft from the roof ring create an amber/cobalt dialogue across his face. A little soft hearth haze creates depth, but no embers flying into faces. A rolled leather map tied with cord sits untouched at the far edge, no readable text. Art direction: bronze, dark umber, deep ink blue, richly tactile silhouette. Bold elegantly condensed warm-ivory cinema title across lower fifth, chapter label CHAPTER II — GENGHIS KHAN beneath, ANDRE ATHAR near top. An intimate, visually electric conversation, not a war poster.
BACKGROUND FACE SAFETY: Absolutely no statues, busts, human sculptures, portraits, paintings of people, mirrors or reflected people anywhere. Architecture, nature and objects only behind Andre.

GALILEO / A QUESTION SURVIVES. Inside the Tuscan stone study, dusty soft-sage plaster, an arched window and a defocused small telescope by the window. Galileo's dark wool scholar gown and broad WHITE LINEN FALLING COLLAR across his near-right shoulder are softly blurred, readable as a period garment; entire head cropped offscreen above/right, no beard fragment. Camera from just behind his shoulder, at table height and subtly closer than other posters. Andre is in focus across the table, sincerely animated and warm, mid-sentence with a slight curious half-smile: his RIGHT hand raised at sternum height in a loose precision gesture, thumb and index gently drawing near with the remaining fingers naturally curved, LEFT palm open just above the table, explaining a difficult idea simply. Hands clear of face. A manuscript is turned blank side up. A focused diagonal beam of afternoon light from upper left creates an almost celestial shaft through gentle dust and a soft circular patch on the plaster, entirely natural light, no glowing universe graphics. Warm parchment, sage, smoky blue and small brass highlights. Use airy sophisticated ivory editorial serif title at lower fifth, with CHAPTER III — GALILEO GALILEI as small subtitle; ANDRE ATHAR discreet top. Photographic human connection is the drama.
BACKGROUND FACE SAFETY: Absolutely no statues, busts, human sculptures, portraits, paintings of people, mirrors or reflected people anywhere. Architecture, nature and objects only behind Andre.

NAPOLEON / THE QUESTION RETURNS. Saint Helena: weathered pale colonial room, half-closed shutters, rain-streaked glass, blue-green Atlantic daylight; one shutter casts a diagonal across the wall. In soft focus right foreground, Napoleon's SEATED forest-green wool shoulder/back with fine red piping and worn brass fastening from reference 3. No imperial fantasy cape or battle helmet, no historical head or face. A CLOSED worn unmarked leather book near his hand, with spine text turned completely away. Camera at seated eye level behind his shoulder, Andre left-centre, closer and tenser. Lips naturally parted, brow drawn with empathy, shoulders slightly forward. Both gestures must read clearly and not merge. His face stays true to the photo. Create a finely controlled blue-grey/verdigris image with a thin warm accent reflected from a low candle out of frame. Elegant silver-ivory title, narrow dramatic serif, lower fifth over dark oak, chapter label CHAPTER IV — NAPOLEON BONAPARTE below, ANDRE ATHAR at top. A psychological chamber drama with emotional movement, not a static fashion portrait.

OPPENHEIMER / THE LIMIT OF AN ANSWER. Night in the rough-planked Trinity camp shelter, dark desert and faint storm rain through a small window, a single tungsten pendant creating a pool of amber on oak. The SEATED physicist's soft charcoal herringbone tweed shoulder/back and a hint of off-white collar occupy near-right foreground in mild defocus. Entire head outside upper/right frame; no famous actor likeness, hat or face. Shot over that shoulder with a slightly compressed 65mm feeling: very intimate Andre, face sharp, medium chest-up with both forearms and hands comfortably in frame. Andre is explaining something difficult, mouth softly open mid-sentence, eyes compassionately on Oppenheimer, not blank or posed. LEFT forearm rests on the table, hand relaxed; RIGHT hand hovers low palm-up in a small open gesture that seems about to fall silent. Natural restrained gravity, not anger, not a grin. His hand catches the brightest warm light; cold blue ambient outlines the grey pinstripe shoulder. Near-black, smoky steel, amber, off-white. One closed unmarked notebook and a plain metal ashtray, no writing, cigarettes or brand. Absolutely no nuclear explosion, mushroom cloud, apocalyptic skyline, fire or supernatural effects. Title integrated into lower dark area, beautifully spaced substantial ivory cinema serif. Small CHAPTER V — J. ROBERT OPPENHEIMER beneath; ANDRE ATHAR at top. Make the conversation and the space between the two men carry enormous emotional weight.
BACKGROUND FACE SAFETY: Absolutely no statues, busts, human sculptures, portraits, paintings of people, mirrors or reflected people anywhere. Architecture, nature and objects only behind Andre.
